metric.why: Some operators and older DCIM dashboards report DCiE rather than PUE. Knowing both prevents misreading a 77 percent DCiE as something other than a 1.3 PUE.
metric.target: A 1.3 PUE and a 77 percent DCiE are the same facility.
metric.formula: (IT equipment energy / total facility energy) x 100
metric.definition: The same measurement as PUE expressed the other way round, IT energy as a percentage of total facility energy.

reading.body:
DCiE and PUE measure the same thing in inverse directions, so a 77 percent DCiE equals a 1.3 PUE in the same facility.

Data center operators and older management software sometimes report DCiE instead of PUE. Without knowing the relationship between them, a reader might mistake a 77 percent DCiE reading for a poorly efficient facility when it actually represents a 1.3 PUE, which is reasonably efficient. The formula clarifies the conversion: DCiE divides IT equipment energy by total facility energy and multiplies by 100, while PUE divides total facility energy by IT equipment energy. A facility where IT load is 77 percent of total energy use has a PUE of 1.3, meaning 30 percent of power goes to cooling, power distribution, and other overhead.

For AI workloads, this distinction matters because PUE variation across data center fleets directly affects how much total power scales require. Two operators reporting equivalent efficiency through different metrics might fail to notice a mismatch in their infrastructure planning. The data does not indicate which metric is more widely used today or whether DCiE reporting is still common in modern facilities.
